title: Neural Network Architecture Builder
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Build a fully connected neural network by adding layers and setting their sizes, and watch the diagram, the PyTorch nn.Sequential code, and the parameter count change together.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to design a fully connected network that meets a stated input size, output size, and parameter budget, calculate its number of parameters layer by layer, and write it as a PyTorch nn.Sequential model.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Constructive building task with a linked diagram, code listing, and parameter count
keyQuestions: Why does changing one hidden layer change the parameter count of two Linear layers?
Which adds more parameters, one more small layer or a wider existing layer?
Why does a layer of n neurons have n biases whatever the size of its input?
What must the input size and the output size of a network match?
commonMisconceptions: The number of parameters equals the number of neurons (the network [4, 8, 4, 1] has 17 neurons and 81 parameters, because every connection carries its own weight).
The input layer has weights and biases of its own (it only passes the features in; the first parameters belong to the connections into the first hidden layer).
An activation function such as ReLU adds parameters (ReLU has none).
Depth alone decides the size of a network (width matters as much: [4, 128, 1] with one hidden layer has 769 parameters and [4, 32, 16, 8, 1] with three has 833).
assessmentOpportunities: Without the sim, students calculate the number of parameters of a network with layer sizes [10, 32, 16, 1], then decide which change adds more parameters, doubling the first hidden layer or doubling the second, and justify the answer with the formula.
